extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers, FFE State regulators/plan management authorities, Exchange administrators, and health plan compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and implementation criteria for proposed amendments to Exchange/QHP certification, network adequacy, Essential Community Provider (ECP) standards, non-network plan certification, audits/compliance reviews, civil money penalties (CMPs), and related administrative procedures under the Affordable Care Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan sameness and cost-sharing modifications (§144.103; §147.106(e)(3)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the definition of 'plan' at §144.103, a State may permit issuers to make greater changes to a plan's cost sharing while still permitting that plan to be considered the same plan—thus maintaining the same plan ID. Pursuant to §147.106(e)(3)(iv), as long as the variation in cost sharing is solely related to changes in cost and utilization of medical care, or to maintain the same metal tier level (and other applicable requirements under 45 CFR 147.106(e) are met), the modifications could be considered uniform (thus, a viable exception to guaranteed renewability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an issuer modifies cost sharing but maintains the same plan ID, enrollees would be auto-reenrolled and crosswalked according to the crosswalk hierarchy at §155.335(j). This approach reduces regulatory complexity and risk of disruption; issuers could continue using existing benefit packages, networks, formularies, including those paired with former exceptions-process plans for PY 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Provider Access Review Program (State authority and technical capacity) (§155.1050(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY 2027+, FFE States (including those performing plan management) may elect to conduct provider access reviews for issuers' plans that use and do not use a provider network, provided the State demonstrates sufficient authority and technical capacity by satisfying the criteria to be considered to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program described at §155.1050(d)(2)–(d)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS would continue to conduct Federal reviews in States that do not elect or do not demonstrate sufficient authority/capacity. Allowing State-conducted reviews recognizes State-specific demographic, topographical, and provider-supply knowledge and may reduce Federal burden while potentially increasing State costs where capacity is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and use of network adequacy data (time/distance and appointment wait times)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will continue to collect network adequacy data, including time and distance and appointment wait time data, from all FFE issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collected data will be used to conduct Federal network adequacy reviews in FFE States that do not elect to do so or do not demonstrate capacity, or to provide standardized data to States determined to have an Effective Provider Access Review Program to assist in their analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network adequacy review flexibility and state-tailored standards
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-size-fits-all approach to provider network adequacy review is not satisfactory; States may face persistent challenges (e.g., contracting with specialists in remote areas) and geographic/topographical constraints that make uniform time-and-distance standards insurmountable in some areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may innovate and tailor network adequacy standards (e.g., assessing time or distance individually, account for bodies of water or mountainous terrain) to reflect local market conditions, provider supply, and access concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum ECP percentage thresholds (§156.235(a)(2)(i) and (b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to consider medical QHP and SADP issuers to have satisfied minimum percentage ECP requirements if they contract with at least 20 percent of available ECPs in each plan's service area collectively across all ECP categories, at least 20 percent of available FQHCs that qualify as ECPs, and at least 20 percent of available family planning providers that qualify as ECPs (medical QHPs only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reversion to 20% (from 35%) is expected to cause minimal disruption since most issuers exceed the threshold; potential impacts include reduced network size (increasing travel/wait times) and cost savings to issuers that could be passed to consumers through lower premiums.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECP justification requirement modification — contract offer status reporting (§156.235(a)(3), (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify narrative justification requirement so that a network plan applying for QHP certification must include as part of its QHP application the status of contract offers to qualified ECPs available in the plan's service area, rather than an open-ended narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers need not report status for all available ECPs but should report status for all ECPs which the issuer has either included in its network or offered a contract to include within each service area. This aligns with MPMS ECP UI changes and is intended to modernize and streamline data submission and reduce administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective ECP Review Program (State criteria) (§155.1051)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States (including those performing plan management) may elect to perform State reviews of issuer-submitted ECP data if they demonstrate sufficient legal authority and technical capacity to be considered to have an Effective ECP Review Program under proposed §155.1051.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must ensure QHPs include sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs to ensure reasonable and timely access for low-income individuals and those in HPSAs; non-network plans must demonstrate access to ECPs that accept plan benefit amounts as payment in full. States should have ECP requirements established in statute or regulation and comparable to Federal standards (or demonstrate how alternatives achieve comparable access). HHS would consider specific factors at §155.1051(e). HHS will continue to collect ECP data and can provide standardized data to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plan QHP certification criteria (§156.236)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans that do not use a network may obtain QHP certification by demonstrating sufficient access to a broad range of providers in a manner consistent with sections 1311(c)(1)(B) and (C) of the ACA. States are not required to approve non-network plans for sale or certify them; impacts only apply in States that decide to approve such plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-network plans may attract healthier enrollees (favorable risk selection) and should anticipate risk adjustment transfers in premium calculations. They may have lower premiums and therefore affect premium tax credit calculations (e.g., being the least expensive silver plan). Issuers should budget for potential high risk adjustment transfers if reserves are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS audit and compliance review authority for APTC, CSR, and user fee programs (§156.480)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify §156.480 to clarify that HHS or its designee may audit or conduct a compliance review to assess compliance with all requirements related to the APTC, CSR, and user fee programs applicable to issuers offering a QHP in an Exchange; compliance reviews may be as needed or on an annual basis and may be enforced in accordance with §156.805.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated compliance cost per issuer: approx. $607.54 (10 hours business operations specialist + 4 hours compliance officer). HHS estimates ~150 issuers reviewed annually; while there are Federal costs, benefits include more accurate APTC reconciliation and recoupment of overpayments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in imposing CMPs and authority to impose CMPs in State Exchanges/SBE-FPs (§156.805)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §156.805(b) to require HHS to identify the lawful purpose(s) of CMPs when determining amounts and amend §156.805(f) to clarify HHS' authority to impose CMPs against issuers in State Exchanges and SBE-FPs for violations where HHS enforcement is triggered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendments are not expected to impose substantial additional costs beyond current processes; data collection associated with CMP imposition is exempt from PRA requirements. The change aims to streamline compliance/enforcement across exchange types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review of issuer sanctions — ALJ subpoena authority and discovery limits (§§156.903, 156.935)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §156.903 to permit an ALJ presiding over an appeal of a sanction imposed under §156.805 to issue subpoenas (on own motion or at request) if reasonably necessary for full presentation of a case and add procedures for issuing subpoenas. Amend §156.935 to ensure discovery provisions do not apply to appeals of proposed CMPs resulting from audits under §156.480(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAB procedures include subpoena processes; exclusion of discovery for such appeals reflects that information is obtainable during the audit and informal refutation process and from public sources. HHS expects no additional costs beyond current DAB appeal accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Netting of CMPs in payment and collections (§156.1215)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §156.1215(b) to make CMPs assessed against issuers subject to netting in HHS' integrated monthly payment and collections cycle and amend §156.1215(c) so amounts owed by an issuer and its affiliates for unpaid CMPs (after netting amounts owed by Federal Government under program affiliates) form the basis for debt determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendments leverage existing netting processes to streamline collections, reduce back-and-forth payments, and limit administrative burden; no substantial additional HHS costs anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory review cost estimation methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate number of reviewers as midpoint between unique commenters on prior rule (269) and page views during comment period (15,824) = 8,046 reviewers; assume each reviewer reads ~50% of the rule; use BLS wage for medical and health service managers ($113.42/hr including overhead); assume reading speed 250 words/minute leading to 6.54 hours to review half the rule; cost per reviewer $741.77; total estimated cost ~$5,968,281.42.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges uncertainty and invites comment on assumptions (midpoint approach, 50% read assumption). This is the proposed analytic method for estimating reviewer burden and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact analysis assumptions and severability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions are treated as severable and impact analyses/estimates presented separately, with attempts to minimize overlap of individuals affected. Baseline uses internal CMS enrollment, premiums, and APTC data averaged monthly and trended by projected growth in under-65 population and projected growth in NHEA less Medicare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific assumptions include expected average enrollment decrease for 2027 between 1.2 and 2.0 million enrollees compared to baseline, assumed premium increases of 2% (if 1.2M exit) or 3% (if 2.0M exit), and that policy changes (e.g., removing certain SEPs, pre-enrollment SEP verification) help mitigate adverse selection. Comment requested on these assumptions and the severability approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Improvement Strategy (QIS) data collection unchanged (§156.1130)
rubrics_metrics.description: No information collection associated with the proposed QIS policy and no changes proposed to QIS data collection requirements applicable to QHP issuers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on this proposed impact estimate and assumption; indicates no PRA implications from this section.
